question.leadin: Prior to this battle, the U.S. had broken the JN-25 code.
question.text: Name this 1942 World War II battle that resulted in the sinking of four Japanese carriers and the loss of only one U.S. carrier.
question.clue: The illness of William Halsey forced Raymond Spruance to take on an unfamiliar command role in this battle, which saw SBD Dauntless Dive Bombers from the Hornet help sink the Mikuma.

swap.leadin: In 1845, a British flagstaff was controversially cut down in this modern country, sparking a year of war.
swap.text: Name this Oceanic nation consisting of a North Island, South Island, and many small islands roughly one thousand miles east of Australia.
swap.clue: This country's nuclear-free policy was enacted by David Lange, who was prime minister when a Greenpeace ship protesting nuclear tests in Polynesia was bombed in this country.

question.leadin: Give the following the 1840 Treaty of Waitangi [why-tahn-gee].
question.text: The treaty was written by British colonizers and purposefully mistranslated when described to leaders of this ethnic group, which didn't intend to give up all sovereignty to the British. Western contact with these people led to a period of infighting called the Musket Wars.
question.answerHtml: Maori people (prompt on, but do not otherwise reveal, answers related to “indigenous New Zealanders”)
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.text: Cleveland refused to annex this kingdom, which had earlier experienced the overthrow of Queen Li  li  uo  ka  la  ni and the establishment of a provisional government.
swap.clue: Its final ruler was forced to sign Lorrin Thurston's Bayonet Constitution, and this kingdom was succeeded by a republic led by Sanford Dole.

question.text: This man was the President of Hawaii while it was an independent, non-monarchical nation, in addition to owning a fruit company.
question.clue: Lorrin Thurston and John Stevens conspired with this businessman to overthrow Queen Liliuokalani. He was the only president of the Republic of Hawaii.

swap.text: In 1818, thousands of Pacific Islanders in this archipelago tattooed on themselves the name of their King Kamehameha. Kamehameha had earlier passed the Law of the Broken Paddle after uniting this archipelago and moving its capital to Honolulu.
swap.answerHtml: Hawaiian Islands [accept Mokupuni o Hawai‘i; prompt on the Sandwich Islands]
swap.clue: Locals call Las Vegas this chain's ninth island, and this group's Big Island is growing at 42 acres per year due to volcanic activity.

question.text: The First Fleet initially landed at this location, but found it to be unsuitable and sailed to Port Jackson instead. James Cook first made landfall in Australia at this location.
question.clue: Fed by the Georges and Cooks Rivers, its north shore is home to Kingsford Smith airport.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the German colonial empire in the Pacific Ocean.
swap.text: This Pacific island country became a German protectorate after Albert Ellis discovered phosphate mines on it. Its status of abuse by the rest of the world continues, as Australia uses it to hoard unwanted refugees.
swap.clue: In 2016, Iranian Omid Masoumali set himself on fire while in this country.

question.leadin: This treaty was the subject of R v. Symonds and another case brought by political leader Wi Parata.
question.text: Identify this treaty partially crafted by James Freeman and William Hobson and subject to several objections by the local rangatira and cannibalism enthusiast, Moka Kainga-mataa.
question.clue: The Native Land Act of 1862 struck down the land-selling article, which had been the cause of the Wairau incident led by Te Rauparaha.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about military engagements in the Philippines.
swap.text: In October 1944, the Japanese fleet guarding the Philippines was destroyed here, allowing the U.S. to begin retaking the islands.
swap.clue: Admiral Kurita withdrew from this battle which would be the last major action of the Japanese navy until Operation Ten-Go.

question.leadin: The women's Mau movement emerged to oppose colonial rule in this country after the Black Saturday massacre.
question.text: Name this Polynesian country where the Mau movement opposed New Zealand's colonial rule in the late 1920s and early 1930s. This country was colonized after German-backed rebels were defeated in the Siege of Apia.
question.answerHtml: Independent State of Samoa [accept Western Samoa; do NOT accept or prompt on “American Samoa”]

swap.text: Beginning in 1865, many Solomon Islanders were blackbirded to work on the cotton plantations on this island. The Leonidas brought the first indentured Indian laborers to this country where Sir Arthur Gordon established indirect rule.
swap.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

question.leadin: Three layers of coral rock slabs surrounded ancient hills called langi that served as the burial sites of royals from an empire in this modern-day country.
question.text: Name this modern-day country, the center of an empire known as "Tu'i [this country]." This country has its capital at Nuku'alofa.
question.clue: This country lost much of its invested capital when former Bank of America financial advisor and honorary court jester Jesse Bogdonoff lost almost all of the profit it had made selling passports to foreigners.

swap.text: In 1975, Whitlam granted independence to this territory soon after Bougainville seceded as the Republic of the North Solomons. In 1962, Indonesia took over Irian Jaya, the western half of this Melanesian country's main island.
swap.answerHtml: Papua New Guinea [or PNG; or Independent State of Papua New Guinea or Independen Stet bilong Papua Niugini or Independen Stet bilong Papua Niu Gini; accept Territory of Papua and New Guinea; prompt on Territory of New Guinea or Territory of Papua]
swap.clue: This country is home to a dialect known as Unserdeutsch, or Rabaul Creole, reflecting its former status as Kaiser-Wilhelmsland during German colonization.

question.leadin: This ruler won a battle that was so violent that it became known as the "damming of the waters" due to the corpses blocking the flow of the 'Iao ("EE-ow").
question.text: Name ruler who won a decisive victory at Kepaniwai with the help of Welsh cannoneer Isaac Davis. This ruler hired Australian convicts Mela and Black Jack to design the Brick Palace for his favorite queen, Ka'ahumanu ("kuh-AH-hoo-MAH-noo").
question.clue: This ruler who established the Law of the Splintered Paddle after winning battles at Kawela and the Pali Lookout.

swap.leadin: One of these structures known as "A Kivi" was significantly less disturbed than others due to being located inland, with statues on it unusually facing the ocean.
swap.text: Name these large ceremonial stone platforms atop which moai statues were placed.

question.text: The US Navy's victory at the Battle of the Coral Sea foiled this Japanese operation, whose goal was to capture Port Moresby in New Guinea and set the stage for an invasion of Australia.

swap.text: This archipelago was once known as the "Cannibal Isles." The Guinness World Record for most prolifc cannibal is held by Ratu Udre Udre (ON-dray ON-dray), a chief at Rakiraki on Viti Levu in this group, who ate between 872 and 999 people.

question.text: The Counter Revolutionary Warfare Unit was the brainchild of this officer, who orchestrated both Fijian coups of 1987. This man, nicknamed "Rambo," then served as prime minister from 1992 until his 1999 loss to Mahendra Chaudry.

swap.text: During the Vietnam War, Holt and this Prime Minister of New Zealand aided the US war effort per the terms of the ANZUS pact. Nicknamed "Kiwi Keith," this leader of the National Party remains the only New Zealand politician to have served as both prime minister and governor-general.
swap.clue: This man who appointed Robert Muldoon as his Minister of Finance and faced harsh criticism for sending military support to the Vietnam War.
